summary: The root حيف (Hyf) signifies acting wrongfully, unjustly, or tyrannically, especially in judgment. It implies inclining to wrong or deviating from right.
lane: 1 حَافَ حاف حافي , aor. يَحِيفُ , (S, Msb,) inf. n. حَيْفٌ , (S, Msb, K,) He (a judge, or any other person, Msb) acted wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically, (S, Msb, K,) عَلَيْهِ against him: (S:) or, as some say, he inclined [ to that which was wrong ], or declined [ from that which was right ], in his judgment. (TA.) حَيْفُ النَّاحِلِ means A man's giving to certain of his children exclusively of others: he should treat them equally, and not prefer some before others. (T, TA.)

headwords.def: حَافَ حاف حافي, aor. يَحِيفُ, (S, Msb,) inf. n. حَيْفٌ, (S, Msb, K,) He (a judge, or any other person, Msb) acted wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically, (S, Msb, K,) عَلَيْهِ against him: (S:) or, as some say, he inclined [ to that which was wrong ], or declined [ from that which was right ], in his judgment. (TA.) حَيْفُ النَّاحِلِ means A man's giving to certain of his children exclusively of others: he should treat them equally, and not prefer some before others. (T, TA.)
تَحْيِيفٌ تحييف The taking a thing, or something, from the side: and diminishing [ from the side ]. (KL.)
تَحَيَّفْتُهُ تحيف تحيفته تحيفتة I took by little and little from its sides; (S, K;) as also تحوّفتهُ. (S.)
حِيفَةٌ حيف حيفه حيفة A side, or lateral part: pl. حِيَفٌ; (K;) which is likewise pl. of حَافَةٌ. (TA.) [See also حَائِفٌ, below.]

Acting wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically: (Lth, Msb, K: [in some copies of the K, حَائِرٌ is erroneously put for جَائِرٌ:] pl. حَافَةٌ (Msb, K) and حُيَّفٌ (K, Msb *) and حُيُفٌ. (TA.) An arrow declining from the right direction. (TA.) And, as being likened thereto, (tropical:) An impotent man, who does not attain the object of his want. (TA.) The side of a mountain. (K, TA.) [See also حِيفَةٌ.]
بَلَدٌ أَحْيَفُ , and أَرْضٌ حَيْقَآءُ, A district or the like, and a land, upon which rain has not fallen: (Ibn-'Abbád, K:) as though the rain treated it wrongfully. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
